newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-INDIAN SELECTORS RESURRECT CHAUHAN'S CAREER.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIAN SELECTORS RESURRECT CHAUHAN'S CAREER.

text.p: Off-spinner Rajesh Chauhan will end a two-year exile from international cricket during the test series against Sri Lanka but will remain under scrutiny, a cricket official said on Sunday.

Chauhan was cleared for selection by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) last month, after it lifted a two-year ban. He will join the Indian team to play two tests and three one-day internationals against Sri Lanka.
Chauhan, 31, replaces off-spinner Noel David in the squad which lost the Asia Cup final to Sri Lanka on Saturday.
Chauhan, whose bowling action was questioned by the International Cricket Council (ICC), the sport's governing body, has been under a cloud since a 1995 home series against New Zealand.
In May a BCCI panel made up of two former Indian captains, Kapil Dev and Sunil Gavaskar, investigated the charge of throwing and found that video footage of Chauhan in action was inconclusive.
"The selectors have given Chauhan a chance to resurrect his test career but the scrutiny of his bowling action will continue," the official said.
"Chauhan needs to convince the ICC about the correctness of his bowling action. BCCI has asked the ICC to produce conclusive evidence in his case," he said.
Since the ICC raised doubts about Chauhan in November 1995, the BCCI has continued to veto his selection to the national team though the player has continued to enjoy success in domestic tournaments.
Chauhan claimed 34 wickets at an average of 34.95 in 15 tests before being sidelined.

Left-handed batsman Vinod Kambli, wicketkeeper Nayan Mongia and uncapped opener Gagan Khoda were the other players picked on Saturday to join the squad for the series against Sri Lanka, which begins on August 5.
The omission of Kambli and Mongia from the 14-member team for the Asia Cup limited-overs tournament created a controversy with skipper Sachin Tendulkar criticising the selection process.

Mongia has been recalled in place of wicketkeeper Syed Saba Karim, who was preferred for the Asia Cup, while batsmen Kambli and Khoda will complete the 16-member test squad. Four players in the squad -- Robin Singh, Nilesh Kulkarni, Debasish Mohanty and Khoda -- have not played test cricket.

Squad: Sachin Tendulkar (captain), Anil Kumble, Navjot Sidhu, Gagan Khoda, Saurav Ganguly, Vinod Kambli, Rahul Dravid, Mohammed Azharuddin, Ajay Jadeja, Robin Singh, Nayan Mongia, Rajesh Chauhan, Abey Kuruvilla, Venkatesh Prasad, Nilesh Kulkarni and Debasish Mohanty.
